Treat the diagnostic as a transaction at an iteration boundary, with no live backward graph. Deep-copy model and optimizer state dictionaries; separately preserve every parameter’s gradient, including `None`, each module’s `.training` flag, and any mutable state excluded from checkpoints. Restore in `finally`, using in-place model loading to preserve optimizer parameter references. Restore module flags individually so mixed train/eval modes survive. PyTorch warns that uncopied model state dictionaries retain references; zero gradients and absent gradients also produce different optimizer behavior. [Checkpoint guidance](https://docs.pytorch.org/tutorials/beginner/saving_loading_models.html), [gradient semantics](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.optim.Optimizer.zero_grad.html).

Snapshot scheduler and GradScaler state, Python/NumPy RNGs, PyTorch CPU/CUDA RNGs, and every explicit sampling generator. Preserve sampler position or use a cached diagnostic batch without advancing training’s iterator. Restore RNGs last; reseeding alone does not restore their positions. Run AMP audits before forward or after `scaler.update()`, completing the diagnostic scaler cycle before rollback. [AMP checkpointing](https://docs.pytorch.org/tutorials/recipes/recipes/amp_recipe.html), [generator restoration](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.Generator.html). Inside a `no_grad` adapter, wrap the diagnostic forward, loss and backward in `torch.enable_grad()`. Under inference mode, also enter `torch.inference_mode(False)` and recreate or clone inference-created inputs there; enabling gradients alone is insufficient. [Autograd modes](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/notes/autograd.html).

Recommended verification: compare continuation from one snapshot with and without the audit, replaying identical batches and RNG states. Require exact equality of losses, gradients, parameters, buffers, optimizer/scheduler/scaler states and subsequent RNG states under deterministic execution. Restore the original snapshot afterward. This establishes numerical continuation for the tested path; state loading does not reverse tensor version counters, external hook effects or untracked iterator mutations.
